t: The Secretary of Homeland Security, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives of any proposed transfers of funds available under section 9703.1(g)(4)(B) of title 31, United States Code (as added by Public Law 102–393) from the Department of the Treasury Forfeiture Fund to any agency within the Department of Homeland Security:  Provided, That none of the funds identified for such a transfer may be obligated until the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives approve the proposed transfers.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "in consultation with" and the requirement of committee approval amount to participation. Every actor here is inside the federal government: two cabinet secretaries consulting each other, and congressional appropriations committees being notified and giving approval. No state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public is brought into the transfer decision, so this is intra-government coordination and not participation.
fable.s: The Secretary of Homeland Security, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives of any proposed transfers of funds

opus.w: The consultation is between two federal cabinet secretaries, and the notice and approval go to congressional committees. Both are inside the federal government. The section has procedural words like "consultation" and committee "approve," but no one outside the federal government takes part in the transfer decision, so this is not participation.
opus.s: The Secretary of Homeland Security, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives of any proposed transfers of funds
opus.b:
1. **Analysis.** The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section requires consultation ("in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury") and committee approval before funds can be spent. That reading fails the definition. Everyone involved is inside the federal government: the Secretary of Homeland Security, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Senate and House Appropriations Committees. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public takes part.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: The section requires consultation between two federal cabinet secretaries (Homeland Security and Treasury) and notification/approval from Congressional committees. According to the definition, both federal agencies and Congress are considered 'inside' the federal government. Therefore, this interaction is purely intra-governmental and does not involve any outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of Homeland Security, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives of any proposed transfers... Provided, That none of the funds identified for such a transfer may be obligated until the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives approve the proposed transfers.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying Congress constitutes "participation" because it involves an external check on executive action. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, any interaction solely between federal agencies and Congress is intra-governmental and does not count as participation. The consultation mentioned is between the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of the Treasury, both of whom are federal officials, which is also explicitly excluded as "intra-government coordination."
